chunks: 3 - He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Bilal al-Muhallabi reported to me, saying: al-Nu'man ibn Ahmad al-Qadhi al-Wasiti narrated to us in Baghdad; and Ibrahim ibn Arfah al-Nahwi reported to us - they both said: Ahmad ibn Rashd ibn Khuthaim al-Hilali narrated to us, saying: my uncle Saeed ibn Khuthaim narrated to us, saying: Muslim al-Ghilabi narrated to us, saying:

A Bedouin came to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and said: By Allah, O Messenger of Allah! We have come to you while we have neither a shrieking camel nor a snoring sheep. Then he began to recite: 'We have come to you, O best of all creation, that you may show mercy to us from the hardship we face! We have come to you while the maiden bleeds from her breast, and the suckling mother is distressed from her baby. And the young man extends both his palms in humility, weakened by hunger - nothing bitter nor sweet. Nothing that people eat is left with us, except the common bitter colocynth and the tough saplings. We have no refuge except with you, and where do people seek refuge but with the Prophets?'

So the Messenger of Allah said to his companions: This Bedouin complains of shortage of rain and severe famine. Then he rose, dragging his cloak, until he ascended the pulpit. He praised Allah: 'All praise to Allah Who rose in the heavens and was exalted, and on earth became close - closer to us than the jugular vein.' He raised his hands and said: 'O Allah, send rain that gives relief, savory, productive, abundant, immediate, beneficial, that fills the udder, grows the crops, and revives the earth after its death.' Before his hands returned to his chest, clouds encircled Madinah like a crown. People from the valleys came shouting: We are drowning! The Prophet said: 'O Allah, around us and not upon us.' The clouds dissipated.

The Messenger of Allah smiled and said: How excellent was Abu Talib! Had he been alive, his eyes would have been delighted. Who will recite his verses to us? Umar ibn al-Khattab stood and said: Perhaps you mean: 'No she-camel has carried a load more kind and dutiful than Muhammad.' The Prophet said: This is not from Abu Talib, but from Hassan ibn Thabit. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib stood and said: Perhaps you mean: 'And the bright one by whose face clouds pour forth - sustainer of orphans, protector of widows. The destitute of Banu Hashim take refuge with him. You have lied, by the House of Allah! We shall not abandon Muhammad and we have not yet stopped fighting for him. We shall not surrender him until we are struck down around him, unmindful of our children and wives.' The Prophet said: Yes. Then a man from Kinanah stood and recited praise for the Prophet's rain miracle, affirming Abu Talib's words. The Prophet said: May Allah lodge you, O Kinani, for every couplet in a chamber in Paradise.

key_terms.إستسقاء: Prayer for rain (istisqa), a special prophetic supplication
key_terms.المنبر: The pulpit from which the Prophet addressed the community
key_terms.حبل الوريد: The jugular vein - a Quranic expression (50:16) for God's extreme closeness
key_terms.غيث: Rain, specifically life-giving rain sent as divine relief
key_terms.يستسقى الغمام بوجهه: The clouds are made to pour by his face - Abu Talib's famous description of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the Prophet Muhammad's prayer for rain (istisqa) and Abu Talib's poem?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Mufid narrates the famous incident of the Prophet Muhammad's prayer for rain (salat al-istisqa), when a Bedouin Arab came seeking relief from severe drought. The Prophet ascended the pulpit, praised Allah with words echoing Quran 50:16 about divine closeness, and made a comprehensive supplication for rain that was immediately answered with miraculous downpours. The narrative is particularly significant in Shia tradition because it concludes with Imam Ali (AS) being the one who correctly identified Abu Talib's famous poem praising the Prophet - the verses about seeking rain through the Prophet's blessed face - while Umar ibn al-Khattab misattributed the verse to Hassan ibn Thabit.
